summary: Magazine-style position paper arguing that digital twins, borrowed from manufacturing and other industries, can support the design, deployment and operation of 5G and beyond networks.
key_result: Frames the network digital twin as an AI-assisted tool for planning and operating 5G and outlines its expected benefits and open challenges, without quantitative results.
limitation_or_critique: Early vision article with no implementation, no fidelity metric and no specific treatment of the core control plane.

expected_title: Digital Twins for 5G Networks: A Modeling and Deployment Methodology
summary: Proposes a methodology and architecture to build and operate a mobile-network digital twin of a 5G core environment, covering data acquisition, modelling, use and the bidirectional link to the physical network (B5GEMINI project).
method: NDT design methodology and reference architecture
key_result: Defines an end-to-end life cycle for automatically creating and using a 5G-core digital twin, applied to cybersecurity and Industry 4.0 scenarios.
limitation_or_critique: Methodological contribution; the abstract reports no measured twin fidelity and no prediction of control-plane action outcomes.

expected_title: SCOPE-5G: A Standards-Aligned Synthetic AMF Observability Dataset for Reproducible 5G Core Benchmarking
summary: Introduces SCOPE-5G, an open framework and synthetic dataset of AMF observability data aligned with 3GPP performance-measurement definitions and seeded with labelled gradual-onset anomalies for benchmarking 5G-core methods.
method: synthetic data generation (queueing, diurnal and long-range-dependent load models, sigmoid anomaly injection)
data_or_testbed: synthetic AMF dataset: 21 procedures, 3 slices, 60 days at 15-min granularity; validated against public references incl. Telecom Italia CDR
key_result: Statistical checks against public references show close agreement (Pearson r about 0.98 with Telecom Italia CDR), and replacing gradual with step anomalies raises detection AUC from 0.919 to 0.998, showing step faults overstate detector quality.
limitation_or_critique: Synthetic data at 15-minute granularity that the authors admit cannot replace operator telemetry; AMF-only, with no SBI/SCP-level traces or UE-level procedure outcomes.

expected_title: Network Digital Twin for 6G and Beyond: An End-to-End View Across Multi-Domain Network Ecosystems
summary: Survey of network digital twins for 6G and beyond across RAN, transport, 5G core, cloud/edge, non-terrestrial and quantum networks, with a dedicated treatment of twins of the 5G core.
key_result: Maps NDT use across network domains from academic and industrial viewpoints and lists open challenges, claiming the first in-depth guide to RAN and core twins.
limitation_or_critique: Very broad scope dilutes the core-network part; as a survey it does not quantify twin fidelity or compare control-plane twin designs experimentally.
standards_link: ITU-T Y.3090; IRTF NMRG NDT draft

summary: Short review of the role of AI in 6G core networks, covering AI-native design, automation and security, and the enablers and requirements of 6G core architectures.
key_result: Identifies interoperability, energy efficiency, computational cost and standardisation gaps as the main obstacles to AI-native 6G cores.
limitation_or_critique: Broad, qualitative overview in a niche symposium; no systematic method, no evaluation, and little anchoring in specific 3GPP Release 18-20 features.

summary: Journal presentation of B5GEMINI, an AI-driven network digital twin for 5G and beyond, describing its infrastructure, its AI ecosystem and two ML use cases.
method: NDT platform design + ML use cases
key_result: Shows the twin being used to design ML-based attack detectors and to develop energy-efficient ML components via a modular Digital Map concept.
limitation_or_critique: Platform and use-case description; twin fidelity against the physical network and control-plane procedure behaviour are not quantified (journal companion of the NOMS 2022 seed).

expected_title: Design of an AI-driven Network Digital Twin for advanced 5G-6G network management
summary: Describes the architecture, infrastructure and AI use cases of the B5GEMINI network digital twin for 5G-6G management, with a detailed case of ML-based detection of a DNS-over-HTTPS denial-of-service attack inside a 5G network.
method: NDT architecture + ML attack detection use case
data_or_testbed: B5GEMINI-INFRA emulated 5G network with on-demand traffic generation
key_result: Demonstrates that the twin supports isolated, repeatable experiments for generating training data and comparing detection and mitigation tools without touching the live network.
limitation_or_critique: Focus is security experimentation; the twin is an emulation sandbox, not a synchronised replica, and no what-if prediction of operational actions is evaluated.

expected_title: Digital Twin-Accelerated Online Deep Reinforcement Learning for Admission Control in Sliced Communication Networks
summary: Combines a behaviour-cloning digital twin of a sliced network's admission policy with online deep reinforcement learning so the agent starts from a safe default policy and converges faster in the real network.
data_or_testbed: simulation of a sliced queueing network
key_result: The twin-accelerated online DRL is more stable and converges faster, improving resource utilisation by up to 26.39% over a state-of-the-art DRL baseline while matching long-term revenue.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only and focused on slice admission rather than core NF operations; the twin mimics the policy, not the network, so it cannot predict outcomes of new actions.

expected_title: Digital Twin For 5G Networks and Beyond: Domain Transfer and Network Behavior Classification for 6G Readiness
summary: Builds an open-source digital twin of a 5G network (Open5GS and UERANSIM) that monitors core-network metrics in real time and classifies traffic behaviour with LSTMs trained on twin-generated data.
method: LSTM classification trained in the twin, tested on simulated and real traffic
data_or_testbed: Open5GS + UERANSIM twin; real network traffic for testing
key_result: The twin runs in real time and supports online fine-tuning, but models trained on twin data lose much accuracy on real traffic, exposing a sim-to-real fidelity gap.
limitation_or_critique: Regional conference with a small setup; the accuracy drop is reported qualitatively in the abstract and no domain-adaptation remedy is evaluated.

expected_title: Building Network Digital Twins Part I: State Synchronization
summary: Analyses the delay chain of state synchronisation between a physical network and its digital twin and proposes prediction-based 'negative delay' to keep the twin in near real-time sync.
key_result: Argues that predicting the physical state can offset acquisition, modelling and transmission delays, enabling near real-time twin synchronisation.
limitation_or_critique: Conceptual and generic (not core-specific); synchronisation accuracy is a fidelity proxy but no end-to-end twin fidelity metric is reported.

expected_title: Enabling simulation services for digital twins of 5G/B5G mobile networks
summary: Argues that a digital twin of a 5G/B5G mobile network should offer discrete-event simulation services for what-if analysis, and presents a framework built on Simu5G with lockstep and branching analysis modes.
key_result: Defines lockstep and branching what-if analysis so the twin can anticipate the effect of faults and reconfigurations before they are applied.
limitation_or_critique: Radio-access oriented simulator; core control-plane procedures and the speed of the what-if loop relative to control-plane timescales are not addressed.

expected_title: Digital Twin Driven Service Self-Healing With Graph Neural Networks in 6G Edge Networks
summary: Proposes a digital-twin-based service self-healing mechanism for 6G edge networks that uses GNN performance prediction to detect abnormal links and nodes and to redeploy services away from them.
method: DT + GNN delay prediction + GNN-assisted service redeployment
key_result: The GNN twin predicts flow-level delays accurately, flags abnormal elements, and its redeployment lowers service delay and improves load balance.
limitation_or_critique: Edge/IP-level services rather than 5G core NFs; the twin evaluates redeployment but is not tied to standard NF selection or restoration mechanisms.

expected_title: Knowledge Graph-Based Propagation for Failure Localization in 5G Core Networks
summary: Localises failures in the 5G core by building a failure knowledge graph of NFs, telemetry features and KPIs, compared through a data-driven graph-attention propagation model and a protocol-aware knowledge-driven reasoning model.
method: knowledge graph + relation-aware graph attention; knowledge-guided hierarchical reasoning
data_or_testbed: real-world 5G core telemetry (operator not named in abstract)
key_result: Both paradigms improve localisation accuracy and robustness, with the learned model stronger on prediction and the knowledge-driven one on interpretability.
limitation_or_critique: Short conference paper; the abstract gives no numbers or dataset details, and failure localisation is not linked to a remediation action.

expected_title: Admission Control for 5G Core Network Slicing Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Proposes RL (SARA) and deep RL (DSARA) mechanisms for admission control and resource allocation of network slices in the 5G core, distinguishing core and edge nodes and batching requests in time windows.
key_result: Both mechanisms outperform existing admission-control schemes for core-network slicing in provider profit and resource utilisation.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-based and abstracts the core as compute nodes; no NF-level or 3GPP slice-admission (NSACF) modelling and no safety mechanism for the RL policy.
